title: Fppf covering calculus for algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. For algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], call a set-indexed family $\{f_i:X_i\to X\}_{i\in I}$ fppf if each map is flat and locally of finite presentation on etale scheme charts [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] and the family is jointly surjective on field-valued point classes [def-trf-algebraic-space-jointly-surjective-family]. Etale maps mean representable etale maps as in [def-trf-algebraic-space]. (1) Every jointly surjective etale family is fppf. (2) If $\{f_i:X_i\to X\}_{i\in I}$ is fppf and $v:X'\to X$ is any algebraic-space morphism, then $\{X'\times_X X_i\to X'\}_{i\in I}$ is fppf, using sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. (3) If $\{f_i:X_i\to X\}_{i\in I}$ is fppf and each $\{e_{ik}:X_{ik}\to X_i\}_{k\in K_i}$ is fppf, then $\{f_ie_{ik}:X_{ik}\to X\}_{i\in I,\,k\in K_i}$ is fppf. (4) For families all of whose sources and target are schemes, this definition is equivalent to being an fppf covering of schemes [def-pc-fppf-site]. Empty index sets are allowed precisely over the empty target, and empty covering members are allowed.

source.place: Tag 03Y8 (definition-fppf-covering), following scheme-comparison paragraph; Tag 0DFC (lemma-zariski-etale-smooth-syntomic-fppf), etale case; Tag 03Y9 (lemma-fppf), parts (2),(3).

proof.text: For (1), fix a member $f_i:X_i\to X$ of the jointly surjective representable etale family. Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $V\to X$ and a surjective etale scheme atlas $U\to X_i\times_XV$ [def-trf-algebraic-space, lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Representability and etaleness of $f_i$ make $X_i\times_XV\to V$ an etale scheme map; composing with $U\to X_i\times_XV$ is etale by [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests]. By [def-weil-etale-morphism] this scheme map is flat and locally of finite presentation. Apply [lem-sfb-space-local-properties-chart-test] separately to these two properties to get them for $f_i$. Joint surjectivity is the assumed one, so the family is fppf.

For (2), fix $i$ and put $P_i=X'\times_XX_i$. Choose an atlas $V\to X$, an atlas $U\to X_i\times_XV$, and an atlas $V'\to X'\times_XV$ from schemes. All spaces and pullbacks exist by [def-trf-algebraic-space, lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The scheme map $h:U\to V$ is flat and locally of finite presentation by [lem-sfb-space-local-properties-chart-test]. The scheme $W=U\times_VV'$ maps surjective etale to $P_i\times_{X'}V'$: indeed $P_i\times_{X'}V'=X_i\times_XV'$, and this map is the base change of $U\to X_i\times_XV$ along $V'\to V$. Also $V'\to X'$ is surjective etale, by base change and composition [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests]. The map $W\to V'$ is the scheme base change of $h$, so it is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] and locally of finite presentation by clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. The chart test applied to the target atlas $V'\to X'$ and source atlas $W\to P_i\times_{X'}V'$ proves these two properties for $P_i\to X'$. No assumption on $v$ was used.

proof.text: To finish (2), take a representative $x'\in X'(\operatorname{Spec}K)$. Apply [def-trf-algebraic-space-jointly-surjective-family] to its image in $X$ to obtain $i$, $K\hookrightarrow L$, and $y\in X_i(\operatorname{Spec}L)$ with $f_i(y)=v(x')|_L$. The compatible pair $(x'|_L,y)$ is a section of the sheaf fibre product $P_i$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] and maps to $x'|_L$. This is exactly the extension lift required for joint surjectivity. Together with step 2 it proves (2).

source.place: Tag 03H4 (lemma-points-cartesian), compatible field representatives; spaces-topologies.tex Tag 03Y9 (lemma-fppf), part (3).

proof.text: For (3), fix $i,k$. Choose an atlas $V\to X$, an atlas $U\to X_i\times_XV$, and an atlas $W\to X_{ik}\times_{X_i}U$ from schemes [def-trf-algebraic-space, lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The composites $U\to X_i$ and $W\to X_{ik}$ are surjective etale: each is a composite of a chosen atlas and a base change of a surjective etale map [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests]. Applying [lem-sfb-space-local-properties-chart-test] to $f_i$ using $(U,V)$ and to $e_{ik}$ using $(W,U)$ shows that $U\to V$ and $W\to U$ are both flat and locally of finite presentation. Their composite $W\to V$ is flat by [lem-pc-flat-compose] and locally of finite presentation by [lem-sbc-locally-finite-presentation-composition]. The commutative diagram $W\to V$, $W\to X_{ik}$, $V\to X$ is a presentation of $f_ie_{ik}$ with surjective source chart. Use [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-source-target-properties] to check the two scheme properties are etale local on source-and-target, and [lem-sfb-space-etale-presentation-property-criterion], conditions (2) implies (1), to conclude that $f_ie_{ik}$ has both chartwise properties.

source.place: Tag 03Y9 (lemma-fppf), part (2), omitted proof expanded using spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 0AML (remark-composition-P); scheme Tags 01U7 (lemma-composition-flat), 01TR (lemma-composition-finite-presentation).

proof.text: For joint surjectivity in (3), start with $x\in X(\operatorname{Spec}K)$. The first covering gives $i$, $K\hookrightarrow L$, and $y\in X_i(\operatorname{Spec}L)$ with $f_i(y)=x|_L$. The covering of $X_i$, applied to $y$, gives $k$, $L\hookrightarrow M$, and $z\in X_{ik}(\operatorname{Spec}M)$ with $e_{ik}(z)=y|_M$. Naturality gives $(f_ie_{ik})(z)=x|_M$. Thus [def-trf-algebraic-space-jointly-surjective-family] holds for the composite family. Its index set is the dependent sum of the given set-indexed families, within [def-weil-size-convention]. Step 4 supplies its flatness and local finite presentation.

source.place: Tag 03Y9 (lemma-fppf), part (2); spaces-properties.tex Tag 03BU (definition-points), extension representatives.

proof.text: For (4), [lem-sfb-space-local-properties-chart-test] identifies each extended flatness and local-finite-presentation condition with the corresponding scheme condition. Scheme points agree naturally with field-valued point classes: [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-field] writes each $t:\operatorname{Spec}K\to T$ uniquely as $j_x\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\kappa(x)\to K)$, where $x$ is its image, so $t$ has the same class as $j_x$. Representatives equal after a common extension have the same image point, hence different scheme points cannot have the same class. This identification commutes with scheme morphisms since both send representatives to their composites. Consequently the image-union condition of [def-trf-algebraic-space-jointly-surjective-family] is exactly ordinary joint surjectivity for schemes. With the two morphism properties already compared, the family satisfies precisely the covering definition in [def-pc-fppf-site], in both directions.

source.place: Tag 03Y8 (definition-fppf-covering), following scheme-comparison paragraph; spaces-properties.tex Tag 03BV (lemma-scheme-points), schemes.tex Tag 01J9 (lemma-characterize-points).

proof.text: Finally [def-trf-algebraic-space-jointly-surjective-family] makes the empty family jointly surjective exactly when there are no field-valued point classes in the target. An algebraic space with no such classes has no section over any nonempty scheme: a section would restrict along $j_x:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to T$ at any point $x\in T$ [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-field]. Over the empty scheme there is exactly one section, since [def-trf-algebraic-space] makes it an fppf sheaf and the empty family covers the empty scheme [def-pc-fppf-site]. Thus this space is the empty scheme's sheaf. Conversely that sheaf has no field-valued points. Maps with empty source satisfy the chartwise flatness and local-finite-presentation conditions vacuously, since any source scheme chart is empty, and the scheme definitions quantify over source points [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Such a member supplies no point lift and imposes no new condition. This proves both empty-family and empty-member assertions.
